content.text: All audit, inspection and verification rights in the Agreement run in IBM's favour against MSL; no provision permits MSL (or MS) to audit IBM. No redline is warranted.

input.quote: In order to verify statements issued by MSL and Subsidiaries of MSL and compliance with the terms and conditions of this Attachment 6, IBM or MS may, at IBM's or MS's sole discretion, cause (i) an audit to be made of MSL's and/or MSL's Subsidiaries' books and records and/or (ii) an inspection to be made of those portions of MSL's and/or MSL's Subsidiaries' facilities and procedures reasonably necessary to verify such compliance.
input.rationale: The AUDIT rule targets audit rights exercisable against us (IBM, as Customer). Every audit, inspection and verification right in this Agreement runs the other way and benefits us: Base § 7.0 process audits at MSL's Work Centers (p0163-p0164); consigned inventory audit/inspection (p0909); acceptance/source inspection (p1047); IBM-owned tooling inspection (p1107, p1113); IBM's retained right to audit system/software access (p1136); Attachment 6 § 4.0 additional audit rights over MSL's software installation locations (p1310, p1312, p1314); Appendix A § 4 audits of MSL's books, records and facilities (p1443), which is expressly limited (45 days' written notice, business hours, independent CPA, IBM/MS bears cost absent a material discrepancy, no more frequently than semiannually — p1443, p1448); and MSL's obligation to admit IBM personnel for inspection and inventory (p1551). § 16.14 Records (p0317) is a mutual five-year record-retention covenant only and confers no audit or access right against IBM. Because MSL has no audit, inspection or system-access right against IBM, there is no Customer-side exposure on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, and nothing to redline. We note only that the mutual record-retention obligation in § 16.14 is a housekeeping burden, not an audit right, and would not flag it.
